# Sandboxes

Start sandboxes, run commands in them, and give them packages, users, files and secrets. Sandboxes are known as capsules in Maitento, which is why the calls start with `Capsule`.

**Library:** [Maitento](index.md#maitento), for apps. More in [Capsules](../../../concepts/capsules.md).

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`CapsuleAddUser`](#capsuleadduser) | Creates a Linux user in a running sandbox, and returns the operation's id straight away. |
| [`CapsuleAwait`](#capsuleawait) | Waits until a sandbox run has ended, then returns it as JSON. |
| [`CapsuleAwaitAll`](#capsuleawaitall) | Waits until every one of several sandbox runs has ended, then returns them all as a JSON array. |
| [`CapsuleAwaitAny`](#capsuleawaitany) | Waits until at least one of several sandbox runs has ended, then returns the ones that have, as a JSON array. |
| [`CapsuleCommandAwait`](#capsulecommandawait) | Waits until a command sent to a sandbox has ended, then returns it as JSON. |
| [`CapsuleCommandGet`](#capsulecommandget) | Returns a command sent to a sandbox, with its status and output so far, as JSON. |
| [`CapsuleDefinitionGet`](#capsuledefinitionget) | Returns a capsule, the recipe a sandbox starts from, as JSON. |
| [`CapsuleDefinitionList`](#capsuledefinitionlist) | Lists capsules, the recipes sandboxes start from, as a JSON array. |
| [`CapsuleExec`](#capsuleexec) | Sends a shell command to a sandbox and returns the command's id straight away, without waiting for it to run. |
| [`CapsuleGet`](#capsuleget) | Returns a sandbox run as JSON: its status, what it has mounted, created and installed, and every command sent to it. |
| [`CapsuleInstallPackage`](#capsuleinstallpackage) | Installs a Debian package with `apt` in a running sandbox, and returns the operation's id straight away. |
| [`CapsuleMountSecret`](#capsulemountsecret) | Writes a secret to a file in a running sandbox, and returns the operation's id straight away. |
| [`CapsuleMountVfs`](#capsulemountvfs) | Mounts a file system in a running sandbox, and returns the operation's id straight away. |
| [`CapsuleRemovePackage`](#capsuleremovepackage) | Removes a Debian package from a running sandbox, and returns the operation's id straight away. |
| [`CapsuleRemoveUser`](#capsuleremoveuser) | Removes a Linux user from a running sandbox, and returns the operation's id straight away. |
| [`CapsuleStart`](#capsulestart) | Starts a sandbox from a capsule and returns the sandbox run's id straight away, without waiting for it to be ready. |
| [`CapsuleTerminate`](#capsuleterminate) | Asks a running sandbox to stop, and returns the stop request's id straight away, without waiting for the sandbox to end. |
| [`CapsuleUnmountSecret`](#capsuleunmountsecret) | Removes a secret's file from a running sandbox, and returns the operation's id straight away. |
| [`CapsuleUnmountVfs`](#capsuleunmountvfs) | Unmounts a file system from a running sandbox, and returns the operation's id straight away. |
| [`CapsuleWaitUntilStarted`](#capsulewaituntilstarted) | Waits until a sandbox has started, then returns the sandbox run as JSON. |

### CapsuleAddUser

Creates a Linux user in a running sandbox, and returns the operation's id straight away.

```c
string CapsuleAddUser(guid processId, string username, jsonArray sudoAsUsers)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `processId` | `guid` | The sandbox run's id, from [`CapsuleStart`](#capsulestart). |
| `username` | `string` | The new user's name. |
| `sudoAsUsers` | `jsonArray`, can be empty | Other users this one may run commands as with `sudo`, as a JSON array of names; `"[]"` for none. |

**Returns** `string`: The id of the operation, to wait for with [`CapsuleCommandAwait`](#capsulecommandawait).

A user name is lowercase letters, digits, `_` and `-`, starts with a letter or `_`, is at most 32 characters, and cannot be `root`, `maitento`, `nobody`, `daemon`, `bin`, `sys` or `www-data`. The new user is not signed in to `mt`, which makes it the one to run untrusted commands as ([`CapsuleExec`](#capsuleexec)'s `runAsUser`). Users the capsule always needs belong in its `users` instead.

The change is queued like a command and runs in its turn, with a 5-minute limit; this call returns its id straight away. Wait for it with [`CapsuleCommandAwait`](#capsulecommandawait). The sandbox must be running: after [`CapsuleStart`](#capsulestart), wait with [`CapsuleWaitUntilStarted`](#capsulewaituntilstarted) first. Fails with "Invalid user parameters: …" for a bad name or a sandbox that is not running, and with "Capsule process … not found or not running" for an unknown id.

### CapsuleAwait

Waits until a sandbox run has ended, then returns it as JSON.

```c
jsonObject CapsuleAwait(guid id)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `guid` | The sandbox run's id, from [`CapsuleStart`](#capsulestart). |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The sandbox run, as JSON.

It returns once the run's `status` is `Finished`, `Error` or `Killed`, checking every half second at first, then every 5 seconds. A sandbox ends when its capsule has `autoTerminate` and its commands are done, when it is stopped with [`CapsuleTerminate`](#capsuleterminate), or when it reaches its `maxDuration`. A sandbox nobody stops keeps the app waiting until then. If the app is stopped while it waits, it returns what it has so far.

The JSON is a sandbox run as [`CapsuleGet`](#capsuleget) describes it. Fails with "Capsule process … not found" when there is no sandbox run with that id.

### CapsuleAwaitAll

Waits until every one of several sandbox runs has ended, then returns them all as a JSON array.

```c
jsonArray CapsuleAwaitAll(jsonArray ids)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ids` | `jsonArray` | The sandbox runs' ids, as a JSON array. |

**Returns** `jsonArray`: A JSON array of the sandbox runs.

A run has ended when its `status` is `Finished`, `Error` or `Killed`. One failing does not end the wait, so check each run's status. The same id given twice counts once, and the runs come back in no particular order. Each item is a sandbox run as [`CapsuleGet`](#capsuleget) describes it. If the app is stopped while it waits, it returns what it has so far.

Fails with "At least one process ID is required", "Invalid GUID at index …: …" and "Capsule process(es) not found: …".

### CapsuleAwaitAny

Waits until at least one of several sandbox runs has ended, then returns the ones that have, as a JSON array.

```c
jsonArray CapsuleAwaitAny(jsonArray ids)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ids` | `jsonArray` | The sandbox runs' ids, as a JSON array. |

**Returns** `jsonArray`: A JSON array of the sandbox runs that have ended.

A run has ended when its `status` is `Finished`, `Error` or `Killed`. Usually one run comes back, but more do when they ended between two checks. The same id given twice counts once. Each item is a sandbox run as [`CapsuleGet`](#capsuleget) describes it. If the app is stopped while it waits, it returns an empty array.

Fails with "At least one process ID is required", "Invalid GUID at index …: …" and "Capsule process(es) not found: …".

### CapsuleCommandAwait

Waits until a command sent to a sandbox has ended, then returns it as JSON.

```c
jsonObject CapsuleCommandAwait(guid processId, guid commandId)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `processId` | `guid` | The sandbox run's id, from [`CapsuleStart`](#capsulestart). |
| `commandId` | `guid` | The command's id, from [`CapsuleExec`](#capsuleexec) or another call that sends the sandbox an operation. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The command, as JSON.

It returns once the command's `status` is `Finished` (a shell command exited with 0), `Error` (a non-zero exit code, a failure, or its time limit ran out) or `AbortedOnTermination` (the sandbox ended before the command could finish), so it always returns. A command that fails is a result, not an error: read its `exitCode`, `outputStandard` and `outputError`. It checks often at first, then every 2 seconds, so it returns about as soon as the command ends. If the app is stopped while it waits, it returns what it has so far.

The JSON is a command as [`CapsuleCommandGet`](#capsulecommandget) describes it. Fails with "Capsule process … not found" and "Command … not found in capsule process …".

### CapsuleCommandGet

Returns a command sent to a sandbox, with its status and output so far, as JSON. It does not wait.

```c
jsonObject CapsuleCommandGet(guid processId, guid commandId)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `processId` | `guid` | The sandbox run's id, from [`CapsuleStart`](#capsulestart). |
| `commandId` | `guid` | The command's id. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The command, as JSON.

The JSON holds `id`; `operationType` (`Command` for a shell command, or an operation such as `MountVfs`, `AddUser`, `InstallPackage` or `Terminate`); `command` and `arguments`; `runAsUser`; `maximumDuration` (`hh:mm:ss`); `status` (`Pending`, `Running`, `Finished`, `Error` or `AbortedOnTermination`); `exitCode`; `outputStandard` and `outputError`, each at most the last 65,536 characters, with `outputStandardFullLength` and `outputErrorFullLength` giving the full length when there was more; `failureDetails`; `timedOut`; `isAsync`; and `dateQueued`, `dateStarted` and `dateEnded`. The outputs and the exit code are null until the command ends.

This is the command as recorded: one in a sandbox that has ended can still read `Pending` or `Running` here, where [`CapsuleCommandAwait`](#capsulecommandawait) reports it as `AbortedOnTermination`.

Fails with "Capsule process … not found" and "Command … not found in capsule process …".

### CapsuleDefinitionGet

Returns a capsule, the recipe a sandbox starts from, as JSON.

```c
jsonObject CapsuleDefinitionGet(string name, string namespaceName)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | The capsule's name. |
| `namespaceName` | `string` | The name of the namespace the capsule is in. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The capsule, as JSON.

The JSON holds `id`, `name`, `namespaceId` and `versions`, oldest first: each deploy that changes the capsule adds one. A version holds `version`, `isDisabled`, `additionalPackages`, `users`, `virtualFileSystemMounts`, `secretMounts`, `startupCommands`, `autoTerminateAfterStartupCommands` and `maximumDuration`. [`CapsuleStart`](#capsulestart) uses the newest version that is not disabled.

Fails when there is no such namespace or capsule.

### CapsuleDefinitionList

Lists capsules, the recipes sandboxes start from, as a JSON array.

```c
jsonArray CapsuleDefinitionList(string namespaceName)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `namespaceName` | `string`, can be empty | The name of a namespace, to list only its capsules; `""` for every namespace. |

**Returns** `jsonArray`: A JSON array of capsules.

Each item is a capsule as [`CapsuleDefinitionGet`](#capsuledefinitionget) describes it. Without a namespace, it lists every capsule in the tenant, sorted by name. Fails with "Namespace '…' was not found." for a namespace that does not exist.

### CapsuleExec

Sends a shell command to a sandbox and returns the command's id straight away, without waiting for it to run.

```c
string CapsuleExec(guid processId, string command, jsonArray arguments, string runAsUser, int maximumDurationMs, bool async)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `processId` | `guid` | The sandbox run's id, from [`CapsuleStart`](#capsulestart). |
| `command` | `string` | The command to run: a program, or a whole shell command line. |
| `arguments` | `jsonArray`, can be empty | The program's arguments, as a JSON array of strings; `"[]"` for none. |
| `runAsUser` | `string`, can be empty | The Linux user to run it as: `maitento`, one of the capsule's users, or one added with [`CapsuleAddUser`](#capsuleadduser); `""` for `maitento`. |
| `maximumDurationMs` | `int`, can be empty | The longest it may run, in milliseconds, before it is stopped; `""` for 5 minutes. |
| `async` | `bool`, can be empty | `true` runs it in the background: the sandbox moves on to the next command without waiting for this one. `""` or `false` runs it in turn. |

**Returns** `string`: The command's id.

Wait for it with [`CapsuleCommandAwait`](#capsulecommandawait), which returns its exit code and output. The sandbox may still be starting: commands sent then run, in order, once it is ready. Commands run one at a time, in the order they were sent, except one sent with `async`.

`command` is shell text, run by the user's login shell from `/`: a program, or a whole command line with pipes and redirects. Each item of `arguments` reaches the program as one word, exactly as given, so spaces, quotes and `$` in it are not interpreted.

The default user, `maitento`, is signed in to `mt` as whoever started the sandbox. Run commands you do not trust, such as an agent's, as a user of their own.

Fails with "Invalid command parameters: Capsule process is not running" when the sandbox has ended, with "Invalid command parameters: User '…' does not exist. …" for an unknown user, and with "Capsule process … not found or not running" for an unknown id.

### CapsuleGet

Returns a sandbox run as JSON: its status, what it has mounted, created and installed, and every command sent to it. It does not wait.

```c
jsonObject CapsuleGet(guid processId)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `processId` | `guid` | The sandbox run's id, from [`CapsuleStart`](#capsulestart). |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The sandbox run, as JSON.

The JSON holds `id`; `capsule` (its `id` and `version`); `status` (`New`, `Running`, `Finished`, `Error` or `Killed`); `failureDetails`, when it failed; `dateCreated`, `dateStarted` and `dateEnded`; `virtualFileSystemMounts` and `secretMounts`; `createdUsers` and `installedPackages`; `defaultUser` (always `maitento`); `commands`, every command and operation in the order it was sent, as [`CapsuleCommandGet`](#capsulecommandget) describes them; and `parentProcessId`, the run that started it.

Fails with "Capsule process … not found" when there is no sandbox run with that id.

### CapsuleInstallPackage

Installs a Debian package with `apt` in a running sandbox, and returns the operation's id straight away.

```c
string CapsuleInstallPackage(guid processId, string packageName)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `processId` | `guid` | The sandbox run's id, from [`CapsuleStart`](#capsulestart). |
| `packageName` | `string` | The Debian package's name, such as `sqlite3`. |

**Returns** `string`: The id of the operation, to wait for with [`CapsuleCommandAwait`](#capsulecommandawait).

A package name is lowercase letters, digits, `+`, `-` and `.`, starts with a letter or digit, and is at most 128 characters. Packages the capsule always needs belong in its `packages` instead, which installs them at every start.

The change is queued like a command and runs in its turn, with a 5-minute limit; this call returns its id straight away. Wait for it with [`CapsuleCommandAwait`](#capsulecommandawait). The sandbox must be running: after [`CapsuleStart`](#capsulestart), wait with [`CapsuleWaitUntilStarted`](#capsulewaituntilstarted) first. Fails with "Invalid package parameters: …" for a bad name or a sandbox that is not running, and with "Capsule process … not found or not running" for an unknown id.

### CapsuleMountSecret

Writes a secret to a file in a running sandbox, and returns the operation's id straight away.

```c
string CapsuleMountSecret(guid processId, string secretName, string mountName)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `processId` | `guid` | The sandbox run's id, from [`CapsuleStart`](#capsulestart). |
| `secretName` | `string` | The secret's name. |
| `mountName` | `string` | The name of the file to write it to, under `/mnt/secrets/`. |

**Returns** `string`: The id of the operation, to wait for with [`CapsuleCommandAwait`](#capsulecommandawait).

The secret's value is written to `/mnt/secrets/<mountName>`, which only the default user, `maitento`, can read. A secret name is letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.`, at most 128 characters. A mount name is letters, digits, `_` and `-`, at most 64 characters, and must not already be used by a file system or a secret in the sandbox.

The change is queued like a command and runs in its turn, with a 5-minute limit; this call returns its id straight away. Wait for it with [`CapsuleCommandAwait`](#capsulecommandawait). The sandbox must be running: after [`CapsuleStart`](#capsulestart), wait with [`CapsuleWaitUntilStarted`](#capsulewaituntilstarted) first. Fails with "Invalid mount parameters: …" for a bad name or a sandbox that is not running, and with "Capsule process … not found or not running" for an unknown id.

### CapsuleMountVfs

Mounts a file system in a running sandbox, and returns the operation's id straight away.

```c
string CapsuleMountVfs(guid processId, guid vfsId, guid vfsNamespaceId, string mountName)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `processId` | `guid` | The sandbox run's id, from [`CapsuleStart`](#capsulestart). |
| `vfsId` | `guid` | The file system's id. |
| `vfsNamespaceId` | `guid` | The id of the namespace the file system is in. |
| `mountName` | `string` | Where to mount it, under `/mnt/`. |

**Returns** `string`: The id of the operation, to wait for with [`CapsuleCommandAwait`](#capsulecommandawait).

The file system appears at `/mnt/<mountName>`, owned by the default user, `maitento`, so a command run as another user cannot read it. Its id and its namespace's id come from [`VfsGet`](file-systems.md#vfsget). A mount name is letters, digits, `_` and `-`, at most 64 characters, and must not already be used by a file system or a secret in the sandbox.

The change is queued like a command and runs in its turn, with a 5-minute limit; this call returns its id straight away. Wait for it with [`CapsuleCommandAwait`](#capsulecommandawait). The sandbox must be running: after [`CapsuleStart`](#capsulestart), wait with [`CapsuleWaitUntilStarted`](#capsulewaituntilstarted) first. Fails with "Invalid mount parameters: …" for a bad name or a sandbox that is not running, and with "Capsule process … not found or not running" for an unknown id.

The change is queued like a command and runs in its turn, with a 5-minute limit; this call returns its id straight away. Wait for it with [`CapsuleCommandAwait`](#capsulecommandawait). The sandbox must be running: after [`CapsuleStart`](#capsulestart), wait with [`CapsuleWaitUntilStarted`](#capsulewaituntilstarted) first. Fails with "Invalid package parameters: …" for a bad name or a sandbox that is not running, and with "Capsule process … not found or not running" for an unknown id.

Removes a Linux user from a running sandbox, and returns the operation's id straight away.

The change is queued like a command and runs in its turn, with a 5-minute limit; this call returns its id straight away. Wait for it with [`CapsuleCommandAwait`](#capsulecommandawait). ### CapsuleStart

Starts a sandbox from a capsule and returns the sandbox run's id straight away, without waiting for it to be ready.

```c
string CapsuleStart(string name, string namespaceName, jsonArray vfsMounts, jsonArray secretMounts, jsonArray commands)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | The capsule's name. |
| `namespaceName` | `string` | The name of the namespace the capsule is in. |
| `vfsMounts` | `jsonArray`, can be empty | File systems to mount, as a JSON array; `"[]"` for the capsule's own. |
| `secretMounts` | `jsonArray`, can be empty | Secrets to mount, as a JSON array; `"[]"` for the capsule's own. |
| `commands` | `jsonArray`, can be empty | Shell commands to run once the sandbox is ready, as a JSON array; `"[]"` for none. |

**Returns** `string`: The sandbox run's id.

A capsule is the recipe, declared in `capsules/`; each start gives a new throwaway Linux machine. Wait until it is running with [`CapsuleWaitUntilStarted`](#capsulewaituntilstarted), or send commands with [`CapsuleExec`](#capsuleexec) straight away: they run, in order, once it is ready. The run records this app run as its parent. Stop it with [`CapsuleTerminate`](#capsuleterminate) when you are done, unless its capsule has `autoTerminate`: otherwise it keeps running until its `maxDuration` (10 minutes by default).

The sandbox mounts what its capsule declares. A non-empty array replaces all the mounts of that kind, and `"[]"` keeps the capsule's own. A file system mount is `{ "vfsId": "…", "vfsNamespaceId": "…", "mountName": "data" }`, with the ids from [`VfsGet`](file-systems.md#vfsget), and appears at `/mnt/<mountName>`; a secret mount is `{ "secretName": "…", "mountName": "…" }` and is written to the file `/mnt/secrets/<mountName>`. Mount names are letters, digits, `_` and `-`, and must differ across both kinds.

A command is `{ "command": "…", "arguments": ["…"], "runAsUser": "…", "maximumDurationMs": 60000 }`, of which only `command` is needed. The commands run after the capsule's own startup commands; read their results in the `commands` of [`CapsuleGet`](#capsuleget).

Fails with "Capsule '…' not found in namespace '…'" when there is no such namespace or capsule, with "Invalid capsule start parameters: …" for a bad mount or an unknown user, and when the tenant's plan does not include sandboxes or it is out of credit.

### CapsuleTerminate

Asks a running sandbox to stop, and returns the stop request's id straight away, without waiting for the sandbox to end.

```c
string CapsuleTerminate(guid processId)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `processId` | `guid` | The sandbox run's id, from [`CapsuleStart`](#capsulestart). |

**Returns** `string`: The id of the stop request, a command of type `Terminate`.

The sandbox then ends with status `Finished`. Background commands are stopped, and a command it had not finished, or one sent after the stop, ends as `AbortedOnTermination`. Wait for the end with [`CapsuleAwait`](#capsuleawait).

Only a running sandbox can be stopped: one still starting (status `New`) or already ended fails with "Invalid terminate request: Capsule process cannot be terminated (status: …)". An unknown id fails with "Capsule process … not found".

|---|---|---|

| `mountName` | `string` | The mount name the secret was written under. |

**Returns** `string`: The id of the operation, to wait for with [`CapsuleCommandAwait`](#capsulecommandawait).

The change is queued like a command and runs in its turn, with a 5-minute limit; this call returns its id straight away. Wait for it with [`CapsuleCommandAwait`](#capsulecommandawait). The sandbox must be running: after [`CapsuleStart`](#capsulestart), wait with [`CapsuleWaitUntilStarted`](#capsulewaituntilstarted) first. Fails with "Invalid unmount parameters: …" for a bad name or a sandbox that is not running, and with "Capsule process … not found or not running" for an unknown id.

The change is queued like a command and runs in its turn, with a 5-minute limit; this call returns its id straight away. Wait for it with [`CapsuleCommandAwait`](#capsulecommandawait). The sandbox must be running: after [`CapsuleStart`](#capsulestart), wait with [`CapsuleWaitUntilStarted`](#capsulewaituntilstarted) first. Fails with "Invalid unmount parameters: …" for a bad name or a sandbox that is not running, and with "Capsule process … not found or not running" for an unknown id.

### CapsuleWaitUntilStarted

Waits until a sandbox has started, then returns the sandbox run as JSON.

```c
jsonObject CapsuleWaitUntilStarted(guid processId)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `processId` | `guid` | The sandbox run's id, from [`CapsuleStart`](#capsulestart). |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The sandbox run, as JSON.

It returns as soon as the run's `status` is no longer `New`. That is usually `Running`, but it is `Error` when the start failed (`failureDetails` says why), and can be `Finished` when the work was already done, so check it before you use the sandbox. It checks often at first, then every 2 seconds. It does not wait for the sandbox to end: [`CapsuleAwait`](#capsuleawait) does that. If the app is stopped while it waits, it returns what it has so far.

The JSON is a sandbox run as [`CapsuleGet`](#capsuleget) describes it. Fails with "Capsule process … not found" when there is no sandbox run with that id.
